item.title: In 1973, Montana released a gall fly to control spotted knapweed; decades later...
item.description: Controlling invasive spotted knapweed biologically has initiated an unexpected ecological chain reaction. Gall flies, introduced as a control measure, have turned into a vital winter food source for deer mice, causing a surge in their populations and an uptick in hantavirus spread. Areas dense with knapweed report more infected mice than those with native grasslands. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Hidden gut bacteria populations linked to ageing, cancer and type 2 diabetes may spread worldwide
item.description: Scientists led by the University of Vienna have found hidden populations within common gut bacteria, some of which are linked to ageing, colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease and type 2 diabetes. The study also found evidence that certain bacterial populations can spread between people and across continents within a few decades, suggesting the gut microbiome may be more transmissible and dynamic than previously thought. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Inside a $25 million Florida mansion with AI controls and 150 feet of Boca Raton waterfront
item.description: An exquisite mansion in Boca Raton exemplifies the pinnacle of luxury living through cutting-edge AI integration. This stunning waterfront property marries sleek modern design with comprehensive smart-home technology, allowing residents to seamlessly control lighting, audio, and climate via voice commands. With six spacious bedrooms and a resort-style outdoor entertainment area, this home is a testament to the transformative power of technology in the luxury real estate market. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Mum of five repeatedly begged for medication in custody, inquest hears
item.description: A First Nations mother of five repeatedly begged prison officials for her medications and was discharged from hospital after a suicide attempt without a mental health review, a coronial inquest heard today. The inquest will look at whether the healthcare she received met community standards. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Meet Benjamin Choi, 17-year-old who built a $300 mind-controlled prosthetic arm that reads brainwaves through non-invasive electrodes
item.description: Benjamin Choi developed an accessible prosthetic arm during the pandemic. This device interprets brain waves and head gestures for control. His invention significantly reduces the cost of advanced prosthetic limbs. Choi's work earned him recognition and funding for further research. He continues to advance machine learning applications in his career. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
